newsitem.title: INDIA: India's BJP urges president not to rush budget.
newsitem.headline: India's BJP urges president not to rush budget.

text.p: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday urged President Shankar Dayal Sharma to exhaust all options for forming a new government before calling a parliament session on the 1997/98 (April-March) budget.

The rightwing Hindu nationalist party told the president in a letter that party leaders met earlier on Tuesday and discussed efforts by the defeated United Front coalition to "lever itself back into office".

It said it also discussed "the quite exceptional parliamentary procedure" that political parties agreed on last week and which would entail a special session of parliament between April 21 and 23 to discuss and approve the budget.

The parties agreed on the special session before voting Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda out of office. The agreement stemmed from concern that key provisions of the budget might expire if the climate of political uncertainty persisted.

The president said at the weekend that he would "facilitate consideration of the budget by the house as the circumstances may warrant". It would be up to the president to call the special session of parliament.
The BJP's letter said Sharma should not call the special session until all options for a new government had been exhausted.

"It would not be fair either to parliament, or to democracy, or to the people of India if the special session became just another device to complete the economic agenda of a defeated government," it said.
"That is why, Sir, we reiterate that the special session be called only if the possibility of an alternative government no longer exists," the BJP said.
"If, however, you are examining the establishment of an alternative government, that possibility must be exhausted before the due date of reconvening parliament," it said.
"If, however, a new government is to be formed, the task of completing the financial arrangements should be left to that government."
The United Front was expected to select a new leader this week, probably on Thursday, who would later replace the caretaker prime minister, Deve Gowda.
